section_summary: This section covers American loans, commercial credits, investments, and blocked funds in Japan during the war in China. It includes consular reporting on American companies, State Department correspondence about loans and credits, telegrams on gold shipments, and a dispute over missing Japanese bonds. The final pages begin an English translation of Japan’s 1938–39 budget, which continues beyond page 80.

subfiles.title: Request for information on loans and credits to Japan
subfiles.about: Jewett asks for information on recent loans and credits to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests figures on loans and credits to Japan during the preceding nine months.

subfiles.title: Reply to Mrs. Jewett on Japanese loans and credits
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department reports no known Japanese loans in the United States and limited information on ordinary commercial credits.
subfiles.summary: Says no Japanese loans are known and distinguishes ordinary trade credits.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on American firms’ blocked funds in Japan
subfiles.about: A division memorandum summarizes Consul Boyce’s reporting on Ford, Singer, and Standard Vacuum in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ford bought Japanese bonds before receiving permits to transfer blocked funds. Singer also obtained remittance permits; American firms shortened credit terms and reduced inventories amid concern about yen depreciation.

subfiles.title: Conversations with American business representatives regarding Japan and the China incident
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Boyce reports on blocked American funds, Japanese exchange permits, bond purchases, and changing business credit practices.
subfiles.summary: Ford’s purchase of Japanese incident bonds preceded permits to remit substantial blocked funds. Representatives of Ford, Singer, Standard Vacuum, and National City Bank discuss exchange controls and possible Japanese efforts to attract American capital for expansion in China and Manchukuo. Firms reduced inventories and credit exposure because of the risk of yen depreciation.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Singer Sewing Machine Company in Japan
subfiles.about: The memorandum extracts earlier reporting on Singer’s Japanese assets, remittances, imports, and refusal to buy incident bonds.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Singer’s approximately ¥22 million in Japanese assets, its permit to remit 1937 profits, reduced installment terms, and refusal to buy incident bonds.

subfiles.title: File note on survey of Japan’s economic position
subfiles.about: The note refers to a memorandum by Stinebower surveying Japan’s economic position.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Stinebower’s brief survey of Japan’s economic position.

subfiles.title: Request for information on loans and investments in China and Japan
subfiles.about: Schorr asks about foreign loans, equipment shipments, and investment interests in China and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests figures for loans, equipment shipments, and American and British investments.

subfiles.title: Updated figures for American direct investment in China and Japan
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: The adviser supplies newly published 1936 investment figures for a draft reply to Schorr.
subfiles.summary: Cites a Commerce Department bulletin reporting 1936 American direct investment of about $90.6 million in China and $46.7 million in Japan, with an explanation of the China estimate.

subfiles.title: Reply to Alvin L. Schorr on loans and foreign investments
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department answers Schorr’s questions on wartime loans, trade credits, and investments in China and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports no known new Japanese or Chinese loans in the United States since July 1937 and no comprehensive figures for foreign commercial credits. Provides American investment figures and refers Schorr to C. F. Remer’s estimate of British investments in China.

subfiles.title: File note on Swedish credit arrangements for imports
subfiles.about: The note points to Boyce’s report on credit arrangements for Swedish products imported into Japan and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Boyce’s report based on a conversation with S. K. F. manager Gosta Guston.

subfiles.title: Conversation with National City Bank president on credits to Japan
subfiles.about: Green records discussions with Gordon S. Rentschler and bank counsel about Japanese trade credits and the Neutrality Act.
subfiles.summary: Rentschler describes mostly short commercial credits and says the bank handled few credits for military goods. A May 9 addition records counsel’s assurance that the discussed credits would cease if the Neutrality Act became effective for Japan.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum forwarding bank counsel’s Neutrality Act analysis
subfiles.about: Green forwards a bank memorandum concerning the legal status of commercial credits to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Forwards counsel’s analysis of Japanese trade credits under the Neutrality Act.

subfiles.title: Bank memorandum on letters of credit and the Neutrality Act
subfiles.about: Stevenson explains the bank’s Neutrality Act clause in its letters of credit and relevant statutory provisions.
subfiles.summary: Describes a clause making credits conditional on lawful shipments and quotes the Act’s financial restrictions and exception for ordinary commercial credits. A postscript explains concern that shipping documents might give the bank an interest in goods under the cash-and-carry provision.

subfiles.title: Hankou telegram on reports of an Anglo-American credit restriction
subfiles.about: Johnson relays a newspaper report alleging that Britain and America planned to restrict credits to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports the allegation and a Commerce Department warning about confirmed letters of credit.

subfiles.title: Department reply correcting reports on credits to Japan
subfiles.about: The Department rejects reports of a joint credit restriction and clarifies Commerce’s advice to exporters.
subfiles.summary: Denies the alleged policy and quotes advice to secure confirmed irrevocable letters of credit.

subfiles.title: Current American loans or investment in Manchukuo and Japan
subfiles.from: Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: The memorandum surveys American public securities, direct investment, and commercial credits in Japan and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Finds no substantial new public securities purchases or industrial investment, apart from bonds bought by American firms seeking remittance permits. Discusses existing short-term trade credits, exchange-control risks, and British policy on lending and export credits.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Tokyo about alleged oil-company credits
subfiles.about: The Department requests discreet verification of an allegation that an oil company extended credit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks Tokyo to confirm or refute the reported credits.

subfiles.title: Tokyo reply on Standard Vacuum Oil Company credits
subfiles.about: Grew reports the oil company’s denial that it extended old credit or granted new credit.
subfiles.summary: Relays Standard Vacuum’s denial of the alleged credits.

subfiles.title: Instruction to relay oil-company denial
subfiles.about: The Department asks Hankou to convey the oil company’s denial to the British informant.
subfiles.summary: Requests that the British source receive the company’s statement.

subfiles.title: Request for assistance with missing Japanese government bonds
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, attention Green H. Hackworth
subfiles.about: Siegelstein seeks diplomatic help obtaining replacement Japanese bonds for Oliver D. Hovey’s estate.
subfiles.summary: Argues that the missing-bond claim involves the Japanese government, despite negotiations with Yokohama Specie Bank and surety companies. Requests intervention through Japanese or American diplomatic representatives while the bank seeks instructions from Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Reply on Oliver D. Hovey estate’s bond claim
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department declines diplomatic intervention without evidence that Japan has refused its bond obligation.
subfiles.summary: Says the presented dispute concerns the bank’s indemnity requirement and a surety company’s refusal to issue a bond. Invites further evidence supporting a claim against Japan.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on August gold shipments
subfiles.about: Grew reports three Bank of Japan gold shipments from Kobe to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Lists three shipments of ¥20 million each on August 15, 22, and 23.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of August gold-shipment telegram
subfiles.about: The paraphrase restates Grew’s report of August gold shipments from Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Restates the three reported shipments to the United States.

subfiles.title: Despatch forwarding Japan Advertiser annual review
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew forwards copies of a newspaper annual review of Japanese finance, industry, and commerce.
subfiles.summary: Transmits four copies of the Japan Advertiser’s 1937–38 review and notes the usefulness and limitations of its statistical tables.

subfiles.title: File note on Japan’s financial strain
subfiles.about: The note points to Grew’s report on Finance Minister Ikeda’s proposed responses to wartime financial strain.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references Grew’s report on Ikeda’s June statements.

subfiles.title: Government finance and Finance Minister Ikeda’s proposals
subfiles.about: The excerpt summarizes Ikeda’s statements on financing the war and adjusting Japan’s economy.
subfiles.summary: Ikeda proposes measures for government-bond absorption, production, exports, capital allocation, consumption controls, and selective easing of import restrictions.

subfiles.title: File note on possible sanctions against Japanese securities sales
subfiles.about: The note points to Davies’s telegram on proposed sanctions involving Japanese securities.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references discussion of sanctions on securities sales and supplies.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram on proposed sanctions against Japan
subfiles.about: Davies reports Litvinov’s account of discussions about coordinated sanctions against Japan.
subfiles.summary: Litvinov recounts a Geneva meeting that considered restricting Japanese sales of securities in China and Manchuria and limiting supplies, especially oil. He doubts coordinated action can be secured.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on September gold shipments
subfiles.about: Grew reports planned gold shipments from Kobe to the United States on September 3 and 6.
subfiles.summary: Lists two planned shipments of ¥20 million each.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of September gold-shipment telegram
subfiles.about: The paraphrase restates Grew’s report of September gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: Restates the two planned shipments to the United States.

subfiles.title: Despatch forwarding Japan’s 1938–39 budget
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew transmits an English translation of Japan’s 1938–39 government budget and lists its enclosures.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the general budget and related schedules for the fiscal year ending March 1939; the separate war-cost budget is excluded.

subfiles.title: Outline of the general account budget for fiscal year 1938–39
subfiles.about: The outline explains Japan’s wartime budget priorities and gives aggregate revenue and expenditure figures.
subfiles.summary: The government plans to curtail nonmilitary spending while funding a prolonged campaign in China. The general account totals ¥2.868 billion in revenue and expenditure, including about ¥694 million to be raised through loans.

subfiles.title: Imperial ordinance relating to the 1938–39 budget estimate
subfiles.about: The ordinance approves the budget and sets limits for Treasury notes, borrowing, and multiyear commitments.
subfiles.summary: Sanctions the ¥2.868 billion budget and authorizes up to ¥500 million in Treasury notes and borrowings under the cited accounting law.

subfiles.title: General budget for fiscal year 1938–39
subfiles.about: The translated budget details Japanese revenues, loans, and ordinary and extraordinary expenditures by department.
subfiles.summary: The revenue tables list taxes, government enterprise receipts, special-account transfers, and ¥694 million in loans. Expenditure schedules detail ordinary departmental budgets and begin the extraordinary budgets, including public works, regional development, financial controls, and wartime-related measures. The enclosure continues beyond page 80.
